body:
The scanner found zero arbitrage opportunities across the 81 live contracts it checked today — a quiet, unremarkable result. That's not surprising given how differently the two venues price gold: Kalshi runs settlement contracts that pay out based on the spot price at a fixed future timestamp (its Above $X series settles September 30, 2026 or year-end 2026), while Polymarket's contracts are mostly touch markets that pay out if gold ever hits a level at any point during a window, plus separate daily up/down bets. Because a settle above price and a touch this level at any point price answer genuinely different questions, the two books can show very different-looking probabilities for the same strike without any real mispricing underneath.

The one thing worth flagging isn't an arbitrage gap but the price level itself: gold is trading in the low-to-mid $4,400s today, which lines up with Kalshi's implied crossover — its $4,370.99 strike sits near even money (bid 0.54/ask 0.57) — and with third-party spot quotes. Gold's spot price was $4,402.89 per ounce as of 9:00 a.m. ET on September 4, and slightly lower than Thursday's $4,489.80, according to CNBC. That level follows a sharp round trip this year: gold corrected roughly 26% from a January all-time high near $5,595 before consolidating back near $4,000, according to Naga, and has since climbed back into the mid-$4,000s.

A few Polymarket contracts show eye-catching bid/ask gaps — for example the September 8 Up or Down market quoting 0.03/0.97 — but these are near-expiry, thin-volume books rather than tradeable edges; a one-sided quote that wide usually just means almost no one is willing to take the other side this close to resolution, not that there's free money on the table.
headline: No arbitrage across 81 gold contracts as Kalshi and Polymarket price different questions
